newsitem.title: CANADA: Molson returns to profit after huge loss.
newsitem.headline: Molson returns to profit after huge loss.

text.p: Canada's Molson Cos Ltd on Wednesday reported net income of C$0.57 ($0.41) a share or C$33.5 million ($24.2 million) in the year ended March 31, 1997.
That compared to a huge loss of C$5.27 ($3.81) a share or C$305.5 million ($220.7 million) in the previous year.
The beer, sports and entertainment company said its fourth quarter net income was nil, compared to losses of C$12.8 million ($9.24 million) in the same period a year ago.
Molson said in a statement its year-end results included a C$79.3 million ($57.3 million) charge related to the settlement of a licensing dispute with American brewer Adolph Coors Co.
The charge was partly offset by a gain of C$24 million ($17.3 million) on the sale of its 45.1 percent interest in Quebec hardware store chain Reno-Depot Inc RD.M.

Molson's turnaround followed a disastrous previous year which saw its earnings hit by a C$270.2 million ($195.2 million) loss on discontinued operations and C$103.5 million ($74.8 million) in charges for real estate losses and restructuring.
Molson Breweries recently reached an agreement with Coors to brew and distribute Coors products in Canada, subject to approval by its minority partner Miller Brewing Co.
Molson Breweries is owned 40 percent each by Molson Cos and Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd and 20 percent by Philip Morris Cos' Miller Brewing unit.
Molson warned on Wednesday that Miller may make legal claims against Molson Breweries or its partners.
"Miller has indicated that it may have possible claims against Molson Breweries and/or its partners," Molson said in the statement.
Molson said that its arrangement with Coors will terminate no later than June 15, 1998 if it has not received approval from Miller before December 31, 1997.
Molson said it realized gross proceeds of about C$1.2 billion ($867 million) from the divestiture of the Diversey group of companies during the year.
